method: Three delegated source reviews; coordinator inspected the central definitions, theorem formulations and representative proof bodies, reviewed scope and exclusions, independently re-read each selected git blob and verified every LOC/hash against the immutable snapshot. No fresh Lean builds or transitive axiom audit.
parent_decisions: Accepted complete generic Group/CommGroup implementations: opposite-side inverse is proved, not an extra missing axiom; additive presentation is supported.

Accepted exact complex Cauchy-Schwarz coverage via real-part/modulus identities; actual core proof is in Defs, public/equality forms in Basic. Excluded weighted Young and operator applications. Tau status inherited, not absent.
Accepted full braided Drinfeld center under only monoidal ambient assumptions. Rejected different categorical centers and extra rigid/pivotal/ribbon center structures.

Accepted separable-closure absolute Galois group with Krull topology. Checked that algebraic-closure and separable-closure groups are equivalent while their ambient fixed fields differ over imperfect fields. Do not credit Tau comparison proof to Mathlib.

Narrowed Tau absolute-Galois selection from seven to three files: Basic/Map/Congr. Excluded fixing-subgroup/finite-index/correspondence/quotient endpoints and their subordinate compatibility files from this bounded core selection.

parent_removed_files.note: Lines 68–110 construct a separable-closure identification for an extension L/K equipped with an embedding into K^sep. Lines 118–193 construct the fixing-subgroup isomorphism with actual continuity proofs. Lines 224–241 compare it with the general restriction map. No finiteness or special arithmetic base field is assumed.

Lines 135–240 package G_L as an open subgroup of G_K along a specified embedding, with index [L:K], for finite separable extensions. Lines 252 onward transport the subgroup maps to the algebraic-closure model, and 392–512 provide normal-extension quotient formulas. This is general finite-subextension API, not a number-field specialization. Whole-file accounting also includes some secondary quadratic/root-of-unity lemmas in the same file.

Lines 34–61 prove compatibility of restriction to normal subextensions with the fixing-subgroup identification. It proves a general group-theoretic naturality square; no cohomology object or arithmetic specialization occurs in the theorem.

Lines 43–69 identify quotients of the named absolute Galois group by fixing subgroups with Galois groups of normal subextensions, as topological groups. Lines 76–113 supply equality-of-subgroup transport and evaluation formulas. The derived opaque Mathlib model requires these dedicated API lemmas.

excluded_candidates.reason: These concern CatCenter C = End(𝟭 C), a different mathematical center; name/path resemblance is insufficient.

Genuine center developments, but add rigid/additive/limit/pivotal/semisimple hypotheses and extra structures beyond the generic core definition. Deliberately excluded from this bounded generic-core/API estimate; not mistaken for absent mathematics. OfHom is a useful builder under LeftRigidCategory and is the closest inclusion-boundary case.
The Drinfeld double-dual isomorphism in an already braided rigid category is not the Drinfeld center construction.

Closure/automorphism-group prerequisite infrastructure and a separate generic topological-abelianization concept are excluded; actual Krull-topology construction is retained because the concept specifically includes that structure.

Universe packaging, pro-p quotients, cohomology/norm constructions, cyclotomic/arithmetic applications and representations on other mathematical objects are outside the bounded general absolute-Galois-group API. The CharacterLattice file contains a small generic action/conversion section, but its main contribution is a separate application; whole-file counting is deliberately not expanded to every such mixed-use occurrence.

specification_findings: Record the full inspected commit independently of the checkout HEAD: the supplied old working checkout has a single AbsoluteGaloisGroup.lean path, whereas the pinned upstream snapshot reorganizes it into a directory. The measurement command currently always reads HEAD, which could count the wrong revision for a reviewed proposal.

A concept can be available through Mathlib while Tau Ceti has genuine native API; distinguish library ownership of files from dependency availability. Center/Basic is an exact example. Pure imports should not acquire Tau LOC or be called mathematically absent.

Equivalent presentations need an explicit mathematical comparison and a record of which library actually proves it. Here algebraic and separable closure models are topologically equivalent, but the fixed fields of their ambient actions differ over imperfect fields. Do not infer equality of descent statements from equality of groups.

Associated API needs a declared stopping boundary. General evaluation/naturality/conversion/maps are retained. Additional structures with new hypotheses (rigid, abelian, pivotal, ribbon center) and arithmetic/cohomological uses are excluded even when adjacent in the same subtree. A filename directory is not the boundary.

Generic constructors instantiated at the desired parameters can establish coverage even without a concept-specific alias. Conversely, a named alias with a different ambient structure does not establish full matching by name alone.

Mixed-use files remain a roughness limit: FiniteExtension contains subgroup API plus some roots-of-unity side lemmas; CharacterLattice/Basic contains a few useful generic action lemmas but primarily builds another object. Record why the whole file was included/excluded rather than silently treating every declaration mentioning a type as API.

Use structured declaration anchors/roles and reviewed mathematical scope in evidence, rather than optional unstructured names only, to make human re-review easier. Do not conflate inspected source with a fresh Lean build.
category-galois.method: Immutable git-archive snapshots of upstream commits; actual source declarations and relevant proofs inspected; no Lean build and no database/library mutations.

Pilot: Group and Abelian group

Scope and immutable revisions
Mathlib: 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970.
Tau Ceti: 3780371ca1bebf9f1c2bb3d753e4bb56c9526023.
Tau Ceti's checked Mathlib dependency: 2ddf59c8f14245864e6c0ed227a2dab76b9efea2 (lake-manifest.json:11).
Queried actual catalogue paragraphs read-only; no identity changes proposed.
Read-only inspection and proposal files only: no DB or repository code edits.

Evidence and file decisions
1. Mathlib group: Defs.lean (Group:33, AddGroup:44, mul_inv_cancel:62, Group.toCancelMonoid:102); Basic.lean (immediate identities in Group section 607–909, including div_mul_div_cancel:739 and integer-power induction:882/899); MinimalAxioms.lean (Group.ofLeftAxioms:39, Group.ofRightAxioms:66, and generated additive counterparts). These implement textbook group axioms and immediate law/constructor API. Group's apparent one-sided inverse axiom does not weaken the match: the other inverse is proved at Defs:62.
2. Mathlib abelian-group: shared Defs.lean (AddCommGroup:111, CommGroup:116, cancellation/division instances:124/129) plus shared Basic.lean (explicit commutative inverse/power laws 516–605, CommGroup-specific division identities 912 onward, mul_zpow:593 and div_eq_div_iff_mul_eq_mul:996). These files genuinely develop both concepts; do not infer sharing merely because abelian groups inherit general-group API.
3. Tau Ceti group: native Pow.lean:58–60 proves a generic integer-power equation rearrangement for arbitrary Group, so the file is direct associated API, even though the definition is inherited. The exact dependency definition was inspected using git show at its pinned commit, rather than assuming the newer standalone Mathlib snapshot matches.
4. Tau Ceti abelian-group: native Pow.lean:50–54 proves a generic integer exponent-vector multiplication law for arbitrary CommGroup; direct elementary algebra API. It shares this 71-line file with group because the file separately contributes to each concept.
No selected source file contained sorry/admit or an axiom declaration; this was a source review rather than a rebuild or transitive axiom audit.

Reviewed exclusions and boundary decisions
- Mathlib Algebra/Group/DivInvMonoid.lean and Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean: parent structures and their generic arithmetic are prerequisites, not automatically all charged to Group. Defs supplies the Group layer over that hierarchy.
- Mathlib Algebra/Group/InjSurj.lean: injective/surjective group and commGroup transport constructors at 281/294/413/426. Legitimate structure-transfer API, but a separate transport task, not needed to implement the catalogue definition plus its immediate laws. Excluded under this pilot's bounded core-law selection; a broader policy could deliberately include it.
- Mathlib Algebra/Group/TransferInstance.lean: Equiv.group:175 and Equiv.commGroup:186 transport structure across equivalences. Same boundary as InjSurj; excluded together to avoid inconsistent class-plumbing expansion.
- Mathlib Algebra/Group/Opposite.lean: MulOpposite.instGroup:163 and instCommGroup:168 implement opposite-group structures, a distinct construction. Excluded rather than automatically mapping every realization of a group.
- Mathlib Algebra/Group/Prod.lean: Prod.instGroup:135 and instCommGroup:180 implement product-group structures; remaining file is primarily homomorphism/equivalence/product API. Distinct construction; excluded from generic groups.
- Mathlib Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean, Hom/Basic.lean, Equiv/Defs.lean, Equiv/Basic.lean: group/monoid homomorphisms and isomorphisms are separate vocabulary. Excluded from generic group/abelian-group mapping.
- Mathlib subgroup, quotient, free-group, group-action, center, conjugacy and torsion trees: distinct mathematical concepts/theorems, not immediate identities defining a group. Excluded.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/Prod.lean: product homomorphisms/equivalences; excluded just as Mathlib product machinery.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/MulOpposite.lean: unopMulEquivOfComm:32 is a generic commutative multiplication/opposite equivalence, not a new group definition or a group-law identity. Excluded along with opposite construction.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/Bool.lean: Bool.cond_cond_inv:26 assumes only InvolutiveInv; specialized Boolean-sign operation, excluded from generic group definition/core laws.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean: map_comp_smul:27 is multiplicative-homomorphism API for bare Mul, not group-specific. Excluded.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/MapMulMulEqOne.lean: MonoidHom.ofMapMulMulEqOne:53 implements homomorphism recognition from ternary relations, while later theorem needs infinitely many squares. Own homomorphism/recognition concept, excluded from generic group.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/AffineSequence.lean: finite sequences with vanishing second differences, a distinct finite-difference result. AddCommGroup assumption is a use, not ownership of all abelian group API.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/IterateOneParameter.lean: its main parameter variable is a Monoid and G a bare type; file placement under Group is insufficient evidence. Excluded.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/Idempotent.lean: conjugating idempotents in a Monoid, its own concept. Excluded.
- TauCeti/Algebra/Group/PowMonoidHom.lean and Primary/: powers subgroups, finite abelian primary decomposition and cardinality statements are separate topics. Excluded.
- TauCeti/ModelTheory/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean: groupOfModel:388 obtains Group from models of a first-order theory. This is a model-theory/group-language bridge, not another generic algebraic Group definition; excluded.
- Tau Ceti Heisenberg/sporadic group instances: specialized group constructions, excluded.

Measurements (physical lines including comments/blank lines, exact immutable bytes)
Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean: 155; sha256 2862e96c66aea952864a5016bb106ca4cf043000a8915d89e24623132e12fb6c.
Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Basic.lean: 1099; sha256 48a12b3df43fb8b5ea5b75677ae93a5f16f9ad9c74dba0befc2ef45b85b1eabe.
Mathlib/Algebra/Group/MinimalAxioms.lean: 82; sha256 f1879a7e70c25a97aa33d22ec026c96d94c7be8c92197d0a1adb9f06cd8e9611.
TauCeti/Algebra/Group/Pow.lean: 71; sha256 ed2d39088183a4cdafea8094190ba2209128e05d4d556f7ef23042733de9e250.
If no other current mappings use them: Mathlib group 709 LOC, abelian-group 627 LOC; Tau Ceti group and abelian-group 35.5 LOC each. Defs/Basic/Pow are mixed-topic files; this is exactly the requested whole-file approximation, not a claim that all their lines prove that concept.

Specification/prompt recommendations
A. Distinguish concept availability from native contribution. A concept can be defined entirely by an imported dependency while a project extends its direct API. Permit positive project status in that case, with dependency source/revision explicit and LOC restricted to project-owned files. If there are no qualifying native files, use an explicit inherited status instead of either 'not formalized' or 'unknown'. Negative judgments otherwise imply falsely that imported group concepts are unavailable in Tau Ceti.
B. Require a declared API boundary. For this pilot: definition plus immediate algebraic identities and equivalent minimal-axiom constructors; stop at products, opposites, structure transport, morphisms, specialized theories and applications. Decide once whether structure-transfer files belong; otherwise agent choices alone vary estimates by hundreds of lines. Do not label file selection exhaustive merely because the definition is formalized.
C. Prevent inheritance inflation. Do not map every Group file to Abelian group solely because CommGroup inherits Group. A shared file needs a direct declaration/section or a specific reason for each mapped concept. Group MinimalAxioms is not added to abelian-group merely by specialization.
D. Require actual statement/axiom comparison. Mathlib's one-sided inverse class definition is equivalent to the catalogue's two-sided definition because the missing side is proved; to_additive creates additive counterparts whose names may not occur literally in source. Searches alone miss both points.
E. Require checked dependency pins. Tau Ceti's dependency is not the standalone Mathlib HEAD and the separate repositories can move concurrently. Review immutable bytes, retain the manifest's dependency revision, and measure those same bytes. Existing 'measure at local HEAD' cannot safely measure a review at an arbitrary pinned commit without a detached checkout or a revision option.
F. Keep exclusions with evidence in a reusable manifest. Future curators need to see why nearby low-level files were omitted, so 'all associated API' does not grow arbitrarily on each pass. These should support the file-mapping judgment separately from the mathematical availability status.

Snapshots
Mathlib: 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970

Tau Ceti's lake-manifest.json pins Mathlib 2ddf59c8f14245864e6c0ed227a2dab76b9efea2. This is NOT the separate Mathlib snapshot. I checked actual declarations at the pinned dependency commit with git show, not merely the manifest.

Concept convex-hull
Catalogue paragraph: The smallest convex set containing a given set of points.
Mathlib full match: Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Hull.lean:48 defines convexHull as the closure operator for Convex, giving exactly the minimum convex superset. Its domain is broader (ordered semiring/module), including the ordinary real vector space case. Lines 52–77 prove extensivity, convexity, universal property, monotonicity and idempotent/fixed-point characterizations; 125–126 identifies a two-point hull with the segment; 155–218 prove image and translation API. No hypotheses making the catalogue concept incomplete.
Additional core API: Combination.lean:256–445 proves finite convex-combination membership and the converse descriptions, with product/Minkowski-sum facts at 453–503. Join.lean:174–181 gives union and insertion elimination formulae. Those deserve inclusion as alternate descriptions and generic constructors/eliminators, despite the distinct auxiliary structures developed in the same files. Under the deliberately whole-file allocation model, all 224+641+197=1062 lines are initially allocated here; the files also contain other concepts, and later mappings will lower this estimate. This is a core-API selection, not a claim that every theorem mentioning convexHull has been inventoried.
Tau Ceti: imported definition/minimum-property verified at pinned Mathlib Hull.lean:49–76. Native generic API exists in TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/Combination.lean:83 (linear bound extends to hull), :96 (a map agreeing with an affine map carries hull onto hull of image), :161 (centroid-interior ray property), :219–273 (affine injectivity on a hull and affine span, preservation of affine independence); :296 onward gives simplex coordinate interoperability. Join.lean:35 gives the generic insertion membership formula without a nonempty hypothesis. These are real native API contributions, not mere downstream usage; map 378+62=440 native lines and never copy the imported Mathlib files into Tau Ceti's path namespace.

Explicit convex-hull exclusions
- Mathlib Analysis/Convex/Basic.lean defines convexity (prerequisite concept); generic ClosureOperator machinery and field/module files are prerequisites, not implementing-file closure.
- Mathlib Analysis/Convex/Caratheodory.lean proves a separate substantial named theorem (dimension/independence bounds), so excluded from this concept's core API map.
- Mathlib Analysis/Convex/Topology.lean concerns convex set topology, closedConvexHull, finite-hull compactness/closedness; distinct topological statements/new object, excluded under the pilot's deliberately narrow core-API boundary. Same exclusion for TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/Caratheodory.lean (IsCompact.convexHull:44 is a completed proof, but a separate compactness endpoint), not because it is absent or unproved.
- Mathlib Analysis/Convex/StdSimplex.lean develops the standard simplex/abstract convex-space interoperability. The finite-combination characterization already appears in Combination.lean; avoid adding all alternative object representations recursively. This is an editorial boundary choice worth exposing to future reviewers.
- Mathlib Analysis/Convex/Extreme.lean and TauCeti/Analysis/Convex/Extreme.lean develop extreme points/sets (different concepts).
- Tau AffineNormalization.lean:143 looks like generic hull membership but is a specific homothetic simplex normalization statement; the file's main result uses maximal-volume simplices/John-type geometry, not core hull API.
- Tau CurveChord.lean:75–93 applies generic hull minimality to curve triangles; a downstream application.
- Tau Geometry/Symplectic/BottSamelson/FixedMoment.lean:366 computes one particular moment polygon's hull; unrelated application.
- Tau simplicial-complex, PL-topology, isodiametric-measure, polyhedral-cochain and Schur–Horn files use hulls for other mathematical endpoints; excluded.

Concept cauchy-schwarz-inner-product
Catalogue paragraph: In a complex inner-product space, |⟨u,v⟩|²≤⟨u,u⟩⟨v,v⟩ for all u,v.
The intended inequality is between real nonnegative quantities: the diagonal Hermitian inner products are real. The current informal formula is conventional but its right side is syntactically complex-valued without that explanation. No identity split is needed; optionally clarify that the diagonal factors are viewed as nonnegative real numbers. Do NOT mark coverage partial merely because Lean makes Re explicit or proves an equivalent norm-product version.
Mathlib proof in Defs.lean:355–374 is a completed discriminant proof on the inner-product core. Basic.lean:280–282 lifts it to public inner-product spaces, with the inequality ‖inner x y‖*‖inner y x‖ ≤ Re(inner x x)*Re(inner y y). Basic.lean:226 proves norm_inner_symm and :207–221 proves real/nonnegative diagonal identities; hence exact equivalence to the squared complex catalogue statement. This is over RCLike, including ℂ; no finite-dimensionality/completeness/nonzero-vector extra assumptions are imposed for the inequality itself.
Mathlib Basic.lean:454 proves the unsquared norm form; :722–845 develops equality criteria, normalized forms, proportionality and unit-vector cases. Those are conventional equivalent formulations/equality API of this theorem, so belong to the same concept. Defs (620 LOC) is essential even though named Defs: it contains the actual proof, not just prerequisite definitions. Basic (1042 LOC) contains public statement and API. Whole-file estimate initially 1662 LOC, acknowledging both files contain much unrelated inner-product structure API and should eventually share allocation with other concepts.
Tau Ceti availability: pinned dependency Mathlib Basic.lean:281–283, :455 and Defs.lean:355–374 were inspected directly, including actual proof. Thus the theorem is available through that dependency.
Native search: searched declarations and references to Cauchy/Schwarz, norm_inner_le_norm, inner_mul_inner_self_le, norm_inner_eq_norm across TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace, plus repository-wide references. No separate generic native implementation of this theorem or its conventional equality API found in inspected hits. Do not classify the theorem as not_formalized in Tau Ceti: it is provided by its dependency.

Explicit Cauchy–Schwarz exclusions
- TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Young.lean:39 is a genuinely proved, three-line CS + scalar Young corollary, but its endpoint is a new named inequality with a free weight ε. Classify under Young's inequality, not every theorem it follows from. This is a useful regression example for stopping 'immediate consequences' from swallowing new theorems.
- TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Contraction.lean:97 is a contraction contact-point inequality with an operator-norm/norm-attainment hypothesis and its own substantial proof; distinct endpoint.
- TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/OpNormDefect.lean:43 is CS for an operator defect form with a new bounded-operator parameter, again a different structured theorem, not a second proof of the generic catalogue concept.
- TauCeti/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/QuadraticForm/TwoVector.lean:67 bounds an inner coefficient using a supplied norm bound; it directly calls Mathlib CS. It is a packaged application intended for block operator perturbation theory, not conventional CS statement/equality API.
- Tau measure/Lp, sphere-cap, Gram/Hadamard, Hilbert–Schmidt columns, weak operator topology, eigenvalue perturbation and energy-estimate files apply CS or prove new endpoints; excluded.

Specification/prompt changes supported by these examples
1. Separate library-owned contribution from availability through dependencies. Add inherited/available_via_dependency with a structured supplying library, the exact dependency revision and precise declaration evidence. Inherited-only records need no native files; a project with a borrowed definition and qualifying native API can remain formalized while attributing definition origin to the dependency and counting only its own files.
2. For every candidate file require evidence of a declared definition, theorem, equivalent formulation, conventional equality case or generic constructor/eliminator/transport API. Finding a use in a proof body does not qualify. File titles such as Defs do not rule out a full proof.
3. Declare the selected core API boundary and explicitly exclude other independently significant named theorems, even short corollaries. Examples: CS equality cases included; weighted Young excluded. Hull membership/finite-combination/image/insertion API included; Caratheodory/compactness/extreme-point and particular polygon geometry excluded. Do not require an unbounded enumeration of all associated results.
4. Whole-file LOC is sample-density dependent: the first mapped concept gets all lines of mixed files. Label the denominator as 'catalogued mapped concepts', not a census of mathematical content. A large number does not mean the theorem itself needs that many proof lines.
5. Review, measurement and dependency snapshots must be pinned independently and consistently. The current measure command's implicit HEAD is unsafe for a review carried out against an older immutable snapshot or a working checkout at a different commit. Accept an explicit revision and verify file hashes/counts against the reviewed revision; do not silently measure newer HEAD.
6. Normalize equivalent mathematical formulations explicitly. In particular complex inner-product inequalities must compare real-valued forms, and importing the same theorem through a broader RCLike statement is full coverage of its ℂ specialization, not partial coverage.

SPECIFICATION FINDINGS
Record the full inspected commit independently of the checkout HEAD: the supplied old working checkout has a single AbsoluteGaloisGroup.lean path, whereas the pinned upstream snapshot reorganizes it into a directory. The measurement command currently always reads HEAD, which could count the wrong revision for a reviewed proposal.
A concept can be available through Mathlib while Tau Ceti has genuine native API; distinguish library ownership of files from dependency availability. Center/Basic is an exact example. Pure imports should not acquire Tau LOC or be called mathematically absent.
Equivalent presentations need an explicit mathematical comparison and a record of which library actually proves it. Here algebraic and separable closure models are topologically equivalent, but the fixed fields of their ambient actions differ over imperfect fields. Do not infer equality of descent statements from equality of groups.
Associated API needs a declared stopping boundary. General evaluation/naturality/conversion/maps are retained. Additional structures with new hypotheses (rigid, abelian, pivotal, ribbon center) and arithmetic/cohomological uses are excluded even when adjacent in the same subtree. A filename directory is not the boundary.
Generic constructors instantiated at the desired parameters can establish coverage even without a concept-specific alias. Conversely, a named alias with a different ambient structure does not establish full matching by name alone.
Mixed-use files remain a roughness limit: FiniteExtension contains subgroup API plus some roots-of-unity side lemmas; CharacterLattice/Basic contains a few useful generic action lemmas but primarily builds another object. Record why the whole file was included/excluded rather than silently treating every declaration mentioning a type as API.
Use structured declaration anchors/roles and reviewed mathematical scope in evidence, rather than optional unstructured names only, to make human re-review easier. Do not conflate inspected source with a fresh Lean build.

File-level exclusions and evidence are in category-galois-proposal.json.
